en: pra, prati, apa, pari, upa, anu, ava, vi, sam, su, ati, ni, adhi, abhi, ā, ud, duri, abhi, āṅ, and upa—these are the twenty prefixes. || 1 ||

Thus end the twenty prefixes (*upasarga*). We shall now state the rules for their application (*vṛtti-sūtra*). *Pra*: this prefix is employed in the following senses: the commencement of an action (*ādi-karman*), intensity (*udīrṇa*), excess (*bhṛśa-artha*), sovereignty (*aiśvarya*), occurrence (*saṃbhava*), separation (*viyoga*), command (*niyoga*), satisfaction (*tṛpti*), purity (*śuddhi*), desire (*icchā*), capacity (*śakti*), tranquility (*śānti*), worship (*pūjā*), the foremost (*agra*), and perception (*darśana*). Regarding the commencement of an action: "The king has set forth" (*pragataḥ*) or "the king is powerful" (*prabalaḥ*).
When it has arisen, the mouse is powerful;
they say "prabala" in the sense of intensity;
"prabhuḥ" refers to Devadatta in the sense of sovereignty.
The Gaṅgā originates from the Himavat upon its occurrence;
he was dispatched during separation;
he was employed in his duty.
Food is consumed for satisfaction;
clear water is used for purification;
and one requests a maiden out of desire.
He is capable in power; he is proficient in knowledge;
the fire is extinguished in tranquility;
he stands with palms joined in reverence.
The sprout is at the front of the tree;
he gazes at the girl for the sake of seeing her—thus is this the prefix *pra*. (1)
*Parā*: [It is used] in the senses of striking, endurance, motion, prowess, facing toward, intensity, lack of predominance, liberation, and opposition. This prefix *parā* occurs in these meanings.
In the sense of striking: *parāghātaḥ*. In the sense of endurance: *parāmṛṣū*.
In going, he has gone beyond;
in prowess, he has exerted supreme effort;
in facing [the enemy], he has turned back.
*Parājitaḥ* is used in the sense of "intensely defeated";
*parādhīnaḥ* in the sense of "subordinate" or "dependent on another";
and *parākṣataḥ* in the sense of "liberated."
In the case of the reverse order, he is turned away. || 2 ||

*apa*: [It is used] in the senses of exclusion (*varjana*), separation (*viyoga*), theft (*caurya*), joy (*harṣa*), instruction (*nirdeśa*), transformation (*vikṛti*), warding off (*vāraṇa*), and reversal (*viparyaya*). This prefix *apa* occurs in these meanings. In the sense of exclusion: "The god was seen away from Sāṃkāśya" (*apasāṃkāśyād dṛṣṭo devaḥ*). In the sense of separation: "He departs" (*apayāti*).
In theft, he steals; in pointing out, he misrepresents; in transformation, he does harm.
The word *vāraṇa* means "removal. In the opposite case, it is an incorrect form (*apaśabda*). || 3 ||

The prefix *sam-* occurs in these senses: conjunction (*yoga*), oneness (*aikya*), origin (*prabhava*), truth (*satya*), all-pervasiveness (*samaṃtataḥbhāva*), ornamentation (*vibhūṣaṇa*), facing toward (*abhimukhya*), connection (*śleṣa*), accomplishment (*siddhi*), and the acceptance of anger (*krodhasvīkaraṇa*). Regarding the prefix *upa-*: it occurs in these senses. In the sense of conjunction: *saṃgataḥ putreṇa* (united with his son). In the sense of separation: *saṃviyuktaḥ priyeṇa* (separated from his beloved).
The authorities declare that identity is primary;
fire arises from wood through production;
this is a true statement.
A conversation takes place in the presence [of others].
In the absence of continuity, it is confused.
A girl is adorned with refinement.
In the sense of being face-to-face, it occurs as *saṃmukham*; in the sense of joining, it forms *saṃdhatte* (he joins) a task;
in the sense of accomplishment, it is *saṃsiddhiḥ* (accomplishment).
In anger, he is enraged;
in appropriation, he seizes. || 4 ||
*Anu*: [It occurs] in the senses of posteriority, following, location, proximity, Vedic study, connection, abandonment, similarity, and direction.
Thus, the prefix *anu* functions in these meanings.
In the sense of posteriority: *anurathaṃ padātayaḥ* (the foot-soldiers follow behind the chariots).
In the sense of location: "The performance [takes place] at Pāṭaliputra.
In the sense of proximity: "The sky [is near] that cloud.
In the sense of study: "He recites grammar."
In the sense of consequence, it is *anuśaya*;
in the sense of permission, one goes having been permitted;
in the sense of similarity, it is imitation (*anukṛti*).
In the sense of facing toward: the calf runs after its mother. In the sense of a mark: he has gone out following that [person].
In the sense of inferiority: the warriors follow behind the leader.

Ava: Regarding the prefix *ava*, it occurs in these senses: understanding (*vijñāna*), support (*avalambana*), purity (*śuddhi*), slightness (*īṣad*), pervasion (*vyāpti*), defeat (*paribhava*), and separation (*viyoga*).
In the case of "understanding," the meaning is "comprehended" (*avagata*) with respect to knowledge.
In the case of "support," one goes while leaning upon a staff (*avaṣṭabhya yaṣṭiṃ gacchati*).
In the sense of purity, *avadātta* means "bright";
in the sense of a slight degree, *avabhukta*;
and in the sense of pervasion, *avakīrṇa* as in "strewn with dust."
In humiliation she laughs at him; in separation, his beloved is cast off.
The prefix *nir* occurs in these senses: separation, intensity, evil, passing away, determination, transgression, and acquisition. In the sense of separation: *niḥśalya* (free from thorns).
In the sense of intensity: *nirnīta* (decidedly).
In the sense of "evil," it means "without restraint";
in the sense of "calamity," it means "going to destruction";
in the sense of "determination," it means "certain."
He is designated by his instruction;
he has gone forth beyond transgression;
and in gain, he is without distinction. || 7 ||

*dur*: This prefix *dur* occurs in the following senses: slightness (*īṣadartha*), censure (*kutsana*), discoloration (*vaivarṇya*), non-attainment (*asaṃpad*), and non-acquisition (*alābha*). In the sense of slightness: *durgṛhīta* (badly grasped). In the sense of censure: *durbala* (weak).
In the case of discoloration, he is ill-favored;
in the case of lack of success, he is destitute;
in the case of non-attainment, he is difficult to reach. || 8 ||

*Vi*: This prefix *vi* occurs in the following senses: manifoldness (*nānārtha*), separation (*viyoga*), excellence (*atiśaya*), fear (*bhaya*), distance (*dūra*), possession (*bhṛt*), purpose (*artha*), strife (*kalaha*), sovereignty (*aiśvarya*), delusion (*moha*), impotence (*pauśunya*), superiority (*utkarṣa*), censure (*kutsana*), slightness (*īṣadartha*), facing toward (*ābhimukhya*), instability (*anavasthāna*), lack of predominance (*aprādhānya*), perception (*darśana*), and heroism (*śaurya*). Regarding manifoldness: "The composition of Pāṇini is diverse. Regarding separation: "separated" (*viyuktaḥ*).
*Atiśaya* means scattered;
*vibhīṣaṇa* means fear;
and *viprakṛṣṭa* refers to a distant path when used in the sense of "slight."
The river is exceedingly pure;
having divided the wealth during the quarrel;
Devadatta has mastery over sovereignty.
Devadatta was despondent in delusion,
agitated by slander,
and astonished by his own excellence.
*Virūpa* is used in the sense of contempt;
*vilopita* in the sense of slightness;
and *vimukha* in the sense of not being face-to-face.
He is bewildered by instability;
he is ruined by insignificance;
the maiden is to be beheld in her vision.
In valor, he is courageous. || 9 ||

ĀṬ: The prefix *āṅ* occurs in the following senses: attainment (*prāpti*), desire (*icchā*), bondage (*bandhana*), fear (*bhaya*), verbal ellipsis (*vākya-śleṣa*), inclusion (*abhividhi*), that which is to be accomplished (*sādhya*), difficult tasks such as penance (*kṛcchrādi-karma*), grasping (*grahaṇa*), location (*nilaya*), proximity (*sāmīpya*), modification (*vikriyā*), invitation (*nimantraṇa*), cessation (*nivṛtti*), benediction (*āśis*), taking (*ādāna*), inclusion (*antarbhāva*), rivalry (*spardhā*), orientation (*abhimukhya*), upward action (*ūrdhva-karma*), astonishment (*vismaya*), establishment (*pratiṣṭhā*), designation (*nirdeśa*), capacity (*śakti*), and limit (*maryādā*).
Thus, the prefix *āṅ* functions in these meanings. For example:
in the sense of attainment, *āsāditam anena* ("it has been attained by him").
In desire, he longs;
in bondage, he puts on armor;
in fear, he trembles.

In the sense of command, one uses *ājñāpayati*. In the sense of inclusion (*abhividhi*), as in "from the worm up to the king," one uses *ākramāram*. In the sense of embracing (*śleṣa*), one uses *āliṅgayati*.
He practices deceit for the sake of his goal;
he has fallen into hardship;
he begins to act for the first time.
In the sense of grasping, it is *ālambate*; in the sense of a dwelling, *āvasatham*;
in the sense of proximity, *āsannam* or *kalyāṇam*.
He relishes in transformation;
he invites in response to an invitation;
he delights in cessation.
In the sense of blessing: *āśāste*.
In the sense of taking: *rasāyanam*.
In the sense of being contained within: *āpītam udakaṃ sikatābhiḥ* (the water is absorbed by the sands).
In the sense of competition: a wrestler challenges another wrestler. In the sense of facing toward: Devadatta comes forward. In the sense of an upward action: the elephant-driver climbs up.
In the sense of wonder, they are "delighted" (ānaṃditāḥ).
In the sense of establishment, it is the "foundation" (āspadam). In the sense of instruction, he "instructs" (ādiśati).
The moon ascends into the sky by its power;
from the boundary established by Āilāvardhana, the rice crops have flourished.

The prefix *ni-* occurs in these senses: settling, heap, intensity, downward direction, dwelling, gate, action, vision, cessation, binding, skill, inclusion, proximity, and liberation as a refuge. For example: *niveśitaṃ* (settled) in the sense of settling;
*nikaraḥ* (a heap) of grain in the sense of a heap.
In the sense of "intensely," it is *nigṛhīta*;
in the sense of "downward state," it is *nipatita*; and in the sense of "dwelling," it is *nivasito naram*.
Devadatta is intent upon the act of giving;
he perceives form through seeing;
he is withdrawn from cessation.
Restrained in bondage;
skillful in dexterity;
water drunk up by the sands within.
In proximity, he is *nikṛṣṭakāla*;
in liberation, he is *nisṛṣṭa*; in refuge, he is *nilaya*. || 11 ||

*Adhi*: This prefix *adhi* occurs in the following senses: subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*), presiding over (*adhiṣṭhāna*), study (*adhyayana*), sovereignty (*aiśvarya*), recollection (*smaraṇa*), and excess (*adhika*). In the sense of subjugation, for example: "The seeker subjugates [it]"; in the sense of presiding over: "He presides over the qualities."
Grammar is studied for the purpose of study;
he is the sovereign lord for the sake of sovereignty;
he remembers the field for the purpose of recollection.
In the case of an excess, it belongs to the king in a superior field. || 12 ||

Also: *api* [is used] in the senses of possibility (*saṃbhāvanā*), cessation (*nivṛtti*), expectation (*apekṣā*), conjunction (*samuccaya*), possibility (*saṃbhava*), censure (*garhā*), benediction (*āśīḥ*), intolerance (*amarṣaṇa*), and inquiry (*praśna*). This prefix *api* occurs in these meanings.
In the sense of possibility: "He might even water a thousand roots. In the sense of cessation: "One might even offer meat as an oblation."

In the sense of dependence (*apekṣā*), this [particle] *atha* is also used by the learned; in the sense of conjunction (*samuccaya*), however, it is "I too" and "this one too"; in the sense of possibility (*saṃbhava*), it is "it is also possible."
(ahiḥ stuhiṣu) one may even revile a low-born person; in the sense of a request, one may ask for rain; in the sense of a blessing, "may you live for a hundred years";
and in the sense of indignation, one may not bow even while serving.
He even wears a necklace as an ornament;
he even goes when asked. || 13 ||

*Ati*: It is used in the senses of excellence (*atiśaya*), intensity (*bhṛśa*), transcendence (*atikrānti*), surpassing (*atikramaṇa*), and increase (*vṛddhi*). This prefix *ati* occurs in these meanings. For example:
"one whose knowledge is superhuman" (*atiśaya*) refers to excellence;
in the sense of intensity: "excessively heated iron" (*atitapta āyas*).
In the sense of surpassing: *atirathiṃ* (one who surpasses the great chariot-warrior).
In the sense of passing over: *hastinātikramati* (he passes over with an elephant). In the sense of increase: *atimeghaṃ gaganaṃ* (the sky is higher than the clouds). || 14 ||
*Su*: [is used] in the senses of respect, intensity, consent, prosperity, praise, and difficulty. This prefix *su-* occurs in these senses: in the sense of respect, as in *susādhu*;
in the sense of intensity, as in *sutaptā āyaḥ*.
In the sense of consent, *sukṛtam*;
in the sense of prosperity, *sumudram*;
in the sense of praise, *sukṛṣim*.
In times of hardship, it is extremely difficult to perform. || 15 ||

The prefix *ut* occurs in the following senses: intensity, separation, upward action, acquisition, manifestation, being unwell, absence of liberation, bondage, predominance, and power. Regarding intensity: *udvilasatsarpaḥ* (a snake hissing intensely).
Regarding separation: *utpathena gacchati* (he goes by a wrong path).
In the case of an upward action, he rises from his bed;
in the case of acquisition, wealth has arisen;
in the case of manifestation, clouds roar in the sky.
Anxious when one is unwell; desiring to depart for liberation; and straying onto a wrong path when [the truth] is absent.
A maiden bound up refers to being tied in bonds; preeminent refers to excellence; enthusiasm refers to capability. || 16 ||

*Abhi*: In the senses of honor (*pūjā*), facing toward (*ābhimukhya*), intensity (*bhṛśa*), similarity (*sādṛśya*), application (*prayoga*), pervasion (*vyāpti*), dancing (*nṛtta*), resemblance (*sārupya*), speech (*vacana*), taking (*ādāna*), and traditional scripture (*āmnāya*). This prefix *abhi* occurs in these meanings. In the sense of honor: *abhivādayati* (he salutes).
In the sense of facing toward: *abhimukhaṃ sthitaḥ* (standing facing [someone]).
In the sense of intensity, *abhirataḥ*;
in the sense of similarity, *abhijñātaḥ*;
in the sense of application, *abhijānāti*.
In the sense of desire, it means "longs for";
in the sense of pervasion, "moistening";
in the sense of dance, "gesticulation."
In conformity, he is well-proportioned;
in speech, he is eloquent;
in taking up [food], he consumes it.
He practices the traditional scripture. || 17 ||

*Prati*: The prefix *prati* occurs in the senses of similarity, taking, non-injury, connection therewith, exchange, substitute, cessation, disease, facing toward, pervasion, and warding off. Regarding similarity: *pratikṛtam devadattena* (a likeness made by Devadatta).
Regarding taking: *pratigṛhṇāti* (he receives).
He repels violence;
he has undertaken its application;
he gives back the ghee weighed out in exchange.
*Praticchandaḥ* means a substitute;
*pratikrāntaḥ* means returned;
*pratiśyāyaḥ* means a cold.
In the sense of facing, as in *pratisūryaṃ gacchati* (he goes toward the sun); in the sense of pervading, as in *pratikīrṇaṃ pāṃśubhiḥ* (strewn with dust);
and in the sense of warding off, as in *pratinivṛttaḥ* (turned back). || 18 ||

*Pari*: [It is used] in the senses of pervasion on all sides (*samantato-bhāva*), narration of faults (*doṣākhyāna*), ornamentation (*upabhūṣaṇa*), worship (*pūjā*), avoidance (*varjana*), embracing (*āliṅgana*), clothing (*nivasana*), disease (*vyādhi*), sorrow (*śoka*), and repetition (*vīpsā*).
This prefix *pari* occurs in these meanings. In the sense of pervasion on all sides: *parikramati* (he walks around).
The village is surrounded by fire in the sense of pervasion;
he wanders about in the sense of reporting faults;
the jar is full in the sense of completion.
He adorns the girl with ornaments;
he performs service as an act of worship;
having excluded the Trigartas, the God of Gods has rained.
In the sense of embracing, it means "he embraces the girl"; in the sense of clothing, "undergarment";
and in the sense of disease, "boils that have spread."
*Paridevana* means lamentation in the sense of sorrow; *parisiñcati* means "he sprinkles" used with distributive repetition (*vīpsā*), as in "he sprinkles tree after tree. (19)

*Upa*: [The prefix] *upa* occurs in these senses: proximity (*sāmīpya*), inability (*asāmarthya*), pervasion (*vyāpti*), acting as a teacher (*ācāryakaraṇa*), pointing out a fault (*doṣākhyāna*), giving (*dāna*), courtesy (*dākṣiṇya*), repetition (*vīpsā*), commencement (*ārambha*), honor (*pūjā*), connection with that (*tadyoga*), excess (*atiśaya*), and death (*maraṇa*).
*Upa* is a prefix (*upasarga*) functioning in these meanings. In the sense of proximity: *upakuṇṭham*.
Devadatta assists in terms of capability;
it is strewn with dust in terms of pervasion;
he instructs the disciples in terms of acting as a teacher.
In the expression of a fault, it means injury;
in giving, it means she brings wealth to Devadatta;
in courtesy, it means polite treatment.
In the sense of repetition: *upayācate*. In the sense of beginning: *upakramate bhoktum*.
In the sense of honor: *upāsitaḥ*.
In connection with that, he speaks of "attained" meditation (*dhyāna*):
wealth attained through a condition;
Devadatta gone to a refuge.
The properties of a prefix apply to a suffix.
Thus ends the treatise on prefixes.
